items.title: Welcome to Google Gemini 4 Argon
items.abstract: A million-token output window changes what you can hand a model in one go, and the benchmarks and the bill show who it actually suits. The post Welcome to Google Gemini 4 Argon appeared first on Towards Data Science .
items.title_ko: Google Gemini 4 Argon 등장 — 출력 토큰 100만 개 지원, 벤치마크·비용으로 적합 대상 가려
items.summary: Google의 새 모델 Gemini 4 Argon은 **100만 토큰 출력 윈도우**를 제공해 한 번에 모델에 넘길 수 있는 작업의 규모를 바꿔놓는다. 글에서는 이 모델의 벤치마크 성능과 비용을 함께 살펴보며 어떤 사용자·작업에 실제로 적합한지를 따진다.

items.title: Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM
items.abstract: vLLM is an open-source inference and serving engine for large language models (LLMs). LLM inference has two distinct phases: prefill, which processes the input prompt and builds the key-value (KV) cache, and decode, which uses that cache to generate output one token at a time. These phases have different compute, memory, and scaling characteristics. Prefill-decode (P-D) disaggregation runs them on separate engine instances, allowing each phase to scale and be optimized independently. This can improve resource utilization, throughput, and latency under load. However, it also requires transferring the KV cache from the prefill instance to the decode instance before token generation can begin, making efficient KV transfer critical to time-to-first-token (TTFT). One of the ways vLLM performs this transfer is through the NVIDIA Inference Xfer Library (NIXL) connector , which moves KV blocks over interconnects that support Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA), such as AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter ( AWS EFA , the low-latency RDMA network used across servers in AWS). On supported instance types , AWS EFA supports GPUDirect RDMA and Neuron Direct RDMA. NIXL can therefore transfer KV blocks directly between GPU or AWS Trainium device memory without staging through host memory. The default mode for NIXL connector is pull-based : After the prefill instance finishes computing the prompt KV cache, the router relays the source metadata, including the prefill block IDs, to the decode instance. The decode instance then allocates destination blocks, prepares the NIXL transfer, and initiates NIXL READ to pull the KV blocks from the prefill instance. Because these coordination and setup steps occur sequentially after prefill and before decoding can begin, they extend the TTFT critical path, as shown in the following timeline. Figure 1: Pull-mode KV transfer timeline, where the router relay, decode-side allocation, and NIXL READ run serially on the path to the first token This post introduces a push-based NIXL connector that moves post-prefill transfer coordination and setup off the critical path. If you run disaggregated prefill/decode inference with vLLM, push mode can improve application responsiveness by reducing TTFT and TPOT, particularly at high request rates. In our benchmark on a 1P1D deployment using Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) P5en instances connected with EFA, push mode delivered up to 3x better TTFT and up to 30 percent better time-per-output-token (TPOT) compared to pull mode (see the Performance data section) for the Qwen3-32B model. Results depend on workload and configuration. We built and validated the feature on AWS Trainium instance clusters connected with EFA, and then we contributed it to vLLM as an accelerator-agnostic feature. The results here are from an Amazon EC2 P5en (GPU) cluster with EFA, showing the gains carry over to GPUs. This post explains the push-based architecture, transfer flow, threading model, performance results, and how to reproduce the benchmark. Push-based KV transfer This section explains the push-based design: its architecture, the transfer protocol, and the threading model that keeps KV transfer off the critical path. Architecture overview Push-based transfer improves TTFT and decode throughput for two reasons: It removes the serialization of the pull model by overlapping producer and consumer work. The decode instance registers its target blocks in advance while the producer is still computing KV. The transfer then begins as soon as the producer’s blocks are ready, rather than after a consumer-side ID-discovery round trip, removing that round trip from the path to first token. It moves the transfer-setup time off the decode instance. That setup runs on the prefill side and on a background thread. It prepares the NIXL descriptors and submits the transfer, so the decode instance does not spend those cycles during its latency-critical token-generation phase. The net effect is lower TTFT and h
items.title_ko: AWS, vLLM용 push 기반 KV 캐시 전송 공개 — EFA 환경 Qwen3-32B TTFT 최대 3배 개선
items.summary: vLLM의 prefill-decode 분리 추론에서 기존 NIXL 커넥터는 pull 방식으로 KV 캐시를 전송해 라우터 중계, 목적지 블록 할당, NIXL READ 요청이 순차적으로 발생해 TTFT 경로를 늘렸다. AWS는 이 전송 조정·준비 과정을 critical path에서 분리한 push 기반 NIXL 커넥터를 소개한다. decode 인스턴스가 미리 목적지 블록을 등록해 두고, prefill 측이 백그라운드 스레드에서 전송 설정과 제출을 처리해 생산자·소비자 작업을 중첩시킨다. AWS Trainium 클러스터에서 개발·검증 후 가속기에 구애받지 않는 기능으로 vLLM에 기여했다. EFA로 연결된 EC2 P5en 1P1D 구성에서 Qwen3-32B 모델 기준 **TTFT 최대 3배**, TPOT 최대 30% 개선을 확인했다.
items.why_it_matters: 분리형(prefill-decode) 추론 구조를 쓰는 대규모 LLM 서빙 환경에서 KV 캐시 전송 지연은 응답성의 핵심 병목이므로, 이를 줄이는 아키텍처 변화는 고부하 상황에서의 실사용 체감 성능에 직접 영향을 준다.
items.whats_different: 기존 pull 기반 NIXL 커넥터 대비, decode 측의 ID 탐색 왕복과 전송 준비 작업을 prefill 측 백그라운드 스레드로 옮겨 critical path에서 제거한 것이 핵심 차이다.

items.title: GenRecs Tokenization: Transforming Ads Recommendation at Meta with Stable Model Vocabulary
items.abstract: Generative Recommenders (GenRecs) represent a paradigm shift from scoring every ad to reasoning about ad content and user preferences together in order to predict the best outcome for advertisers. Leveraging the world knowledge built into LLMs makes ad matching more intelligent and precise, compounding gains for advertisers. GenRecs Tokenization is the foundational data representation that makes this possible. Rather than maintaining a dedicated ID for every item, GenRecs Tokenization represents each item with a set of tokens from a stable semantic vocabulary. Paired with Meta’s Generative Ads Model (GEM) and Meta’s Adaptive Ranking Model , GenRecs Tokenization has delivered a +0.35% lift in conversions across surfaces for advertisers. GenRecs improves the way Meta’s ads recommendation systems make predictions today. Short for Generative Recommenders , GenRecs shifts our approach from scoring every individual ad candidate to leveraging LLM architecture to deeply reason about ad content and user preferences simultaneously. By pairing pre-trained world knowledge with a semantic understanding of what an ad actually represents, the system moves beyond click-pattern matching to understand underlying user preferences. This allows the model to predict the most relevant ad for each person, even when surfacing brand-new products with no past product, ad or company engagement history. GenRecs Tokenization is the foundational data representation that makes this possible. Instead of maintaining a dedicated ID for every concept in the world, language models compose a small vocabulary of semantic tokens to represent any concept. Because tokens describe what an item (e.g., ads, products, services, etc.) is, the model can relate an item it has never seen engagement for, to items it knows well. A newly launched “trail shoe” inherits what the model has already learned about that category, rather than starting a new representation with no signal. GenRecs Tokenization introduces a structured vocabulary approach for ad recommendations, enabling GenRecs for both retrieval and ranking across every item type in the system, including ads, products, pages, and pixels. Meta’s state-of-the-art ads recommendation system drives ongoing advertiser performance improvements by learning about individual items and how they perform . LLMs present a unique opportunity to further improve the performance of recommendation systems by leveraging semantic tokenization in several ads use cases: Accelerating learning from new entities: Semantic tokenization helps models to infer relevance and establish relationships through shared concepts. New entities include newly created ads, niche products, and pages with limited engagement. Enabling cross-campaign transfer: Semantic tokenization creates a stable vocabulary that allows the models to carry insights across campaigns for advertisers. LLM scaling benefits: Semantic tokenization allows the benefits to compound with the LLM scaling curve’s improving performance. Infusing world knowledge: Semantic tokenization gives pre-trained language models a direct interface to reason about ad content and user intent. Once items are migrated to semantic tokens, models learn from token patterns much like LLMs do. In production, this yields: Prediction accuracy improvements in production: Paired with Meta’s GEM and Adaptive Ranking Model , GenRecs Tokenization delivered a +0.35% lift 1 in conversions. Compounding feedback loop: Better tail predictions yield better lessons from tail ads which enrich the training data to further improve predictions for all ads from the model, creating a performance improving feedback loop. A new way to scale: Across production ranking and retrieval, tokens bend the scaling curve along sequence length, training data, and model architecture. 1 Meta Internal Data, measured in February 2026. items.title_ko: Meta, GenRecs Tokenization 공개 — ID 대신 의미 토큰 어휘로 광고 추천, 전환율 +0.35% 상승
items.summary: Meta는 광고마다 개별 ID를 부여하는 대신 안정적인 의미 토큰 어휘로 아이템을 표현하는 GenRecs Tokenization을 도입했다. 이는 모든 광고 후보를 개별 스코어링하던 기존 방식 대신 LLM 구조로 광고 콘텐츠와 사용자 선호를 함께 추론하는 GenRecs 패러다임의 기반 데이터 표현이다. 토큰은 아이템이 무엇을 나타내는지 설명하므로, 과거 참여 이력이 전혀 없는 신규 제품이나 광고도 모델이 이미 학습한 유사 카테고리의 지식을 상속받아 추론할 수 있다. Meta의 Generative Ads Model(GEM)과 Adaptive Ranking Model과 결합해 전 서비스 표면에서 **전환율 +0.35%** 상승을 달성했다. 이 어휘는 광고, 제품, 페이지, 픽셀 등 모든 아이템 유형에 걸쳐 검색(retrieval)과 랭킹(ranking) 양쪽에 적용된다.
items.why_it_matters: 신규 엔티티에 대한 콜드스타트 문제를 의미 토큰으로 해결하면서 캠페인 간 통찰 전이와 LLM 스케일링 이득까지 함께 가져갈 수 있어, 산업 규모 추천 시스템 설계에 참고할 만한 사례다.
items.whats_different: 기존 추천 시스템이 아이템마다 고유 ID를 부여해 개별적으로 점수화하던 방식과 달리, **공유된 의미 토큰 어휘**로 아이템을 표현해 참여 이력이 없는 신규 아이템도 유사 개념으로부터 지식을 전이받을 수 있다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: How Deepgram optimized voice AI at scale with AWS Trainium
items.abstract: As voice becomes a first-class modality for AI, Deepgram’s models span speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and voice agents. They now process quadrillions of audio tokens a year for more than 200,000 developers and 1,400 organizations. Customers use them through the Deepgram API or run them in their own environments, including on Amazon SageMaker AI. For Deepgram, serving efficiency determines how much audio the system can process for a given infrastructure budget. High-volume batch workloads put heavy pressure on that budget, so the more efficiently each accelerator hour is used, the more audio Deepgram can serve on the same fleet. That made inference efficiency a natural target and Deepgram turned to AWS AI chips to improve it. They worked with AWS to bring its Nova-3 speech-to-text model to AWS Trainium2 for offline batch workloads such as contact-center analytics and medical transcription. The engagement began with Deepgram delivering Nova-3 as standard PyTorch code. Over several months, Deepgram and the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team ported Nova-3 to AWS Trainium2 in PyTorch reconstruction and tuned it for the new hardware. The final configuration runs eight model replicas on a single Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) trn2.3xlarge instance. On Deepgram’s offline, throughput-oriented batch workloads, that setup processed 11–70 percent more audio per dollar than the compute options Deepgram had been running. We measured this using instance pricing at the time of the evaluation. These gains help Deepgram scale efficiently, keep shipping better models, and bring them to customers at lower prices. These benefits can extend to customers who self-host Deepgram models in their own virtual private cloud (VPC) on Amazon SageMaker AI. There, Deepgram and AWS continue to improve ease of setup, reliability, and observability. In this post, we walk through the full inference optimization effort on Trainium: porting Nova-3 to the AWS Neuron software stack, the kernel-level tuning that followed, the data-parallel Rust runtime that lets Deepgram’s own model server call Trainium, and the throughput and cost results we measured on batch transcription. Optimizing Nova-3 to Trainium2 with native PyTorch Starting with standard PyTorch code, we used TorchNeuron, the native PyTorch integration of the Neuron Compiler, which supports both eager execution and torch.compile . We ran Nova-3 in eager mode on Trainium2 first and checked which operations fell back to the CPU, then compiled with torch.compile . The compiled path ran every model operation on Trainium2 with no CPU fallbacks detected. We compiled the encoder and decoder as separate static-shape graphs using torch.compile . Throughout, we checked numerical accuracy at two levels: layer-level output consistency against CPU, and the end-to-end Word Error Rate (WER), which had to stay in line with Deepgram’s reference values and target. From that working baseline, we kicked off the optimization work by replacing several layers with fused kernels from the public NKI Library (NKILib), a collection of pre-built reference kernels written with the Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI). The kernels covered operations such as fused QKV projections, fused feed-forward network (FFN) layers, and depthwise 1D convolution. We optimized for throughput and, by extension, cost efficiency, targeting Deepgram’s offline inference workloads. Throughput is reported as a relative gain over a baseline configuration rather than as absolute audio processed per second, and we swept batch sizes 1–128 to find the throughput-maximizing batch size. Kernel-level tuning with Neuron Explorer and NAD Enabling kernels is only the first step of an optimization flywheel: enable an NKI kernel (custom or from NKILib), profile the workload, then either tune the existing kernel or replace it with a new one based on the profiling insights. This cycle repeats until the performance target is met. At each step, a different part
items.title_ko: Deepgram, AWS Trainium2로 Nova-3 음성AI 추론 최적화 — 달러당 처리량 11~70% 향상
items.summary: Deepgram은 연간 수천조 개의 오디오 토큰을 처리하는 음성인식 모델 Nova-3를 AWS Trainium2에 이식해 오프라인 배치 전사 워크로드를 최적화했다. PyTorch 코드를 TorchNeuron과 torch.compile로 컴파일해 CPU 폴백 없이 전량 Trainium2에서 동작하도록 만들고, NKI Library의 융합 커널(QKV projection, FFN, depthwise 1D convolution 등)로 레이어를 교체했다. 레이어 단위 출력 일치성과 end-to-end WER을 기준값과 비교해 정확도를 검증했으며, 배치 크기 1~128을 스윕해 처리량을 최대화했다. 최종적으로 trn2.3xlarge 인스턴스 1대에 모델 복제본 8개를 동시 구동하는 구성으로, **달러당 처리 오디오량이 기존 대비 11~70% 증가**했다.
items.why_it_matters: 음성을 1급 모달리티로 다루는 서비스가 늘면서 추론 효율이 곧 인프라 비용과 서비스 가격 경쟁력을 좌우하는데, 이번 사례는 전용 가속기로 대규모 배치 음성 워크로드의 비용을 실질적으로 낮출 수 있음을 보여준다. SageMaker AI에서 자체 VPC로 Deepgram 모델을 호스팅하는 고객에게도 동일한 이득이 확장될 수 있다는 점도 주목할 만하다.
items.whats_different: 기존 Deepgram이 사용하던 컴퓨팅 옵션(GPU 기반 추론) 대비, Trainium2와 Neuron 소프트웨어 스택(TorchNeuron, torch.compile, NKI 커널)으로 이식 및 커널 단위 튜닝을 거쳐 달러당 처리량을 11~70% 끌어올린 것이 핵심 차이다.

items.title: Accelerating Mamba-2 with High-Performance Forward Pass Kernels in NVIDIA CUDA Tile
items.abstract: NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) is a Python-based DSL and parallel programming model for NVIDIA GPUs that automatically leverages advanced hardware capabilities to... NVIDIA CUDA Tile (cuTile) is a Python-based DSL and parallel programming model for NVIDIA GPUs that automatically leverages advanced hardware capabilities to deliver peak performance for tile-level GPU programming. By abstracting thread- and warp-level scheduling behind high-level, tile-centric primitives, cuTile enables you to write GPU kernels in Python while compiler optimizations automatically… Source
items.title_ko: NVIDIA, cuTile로 Mamba-2 순전파 커널 가속 — Python DSL로 타일 단위 GPU 프로그래밍 자동 최적화
items.summary: NVIDIA CUDA Tile(cuTile)은 NVIDIA GPU용 Python 기반 DSL이자 병렬 프로그래밍 모델이다. 스레드·워프 수준의 스케줄링을 타일 중심의 고수준 primitive로 추상화해, 사용자는 Python으로 GPU 커널을 작성하고 **컴파일러가 자동으로 하드웨어 성능을 최적화**하도록 한다. 이 글은 cuTile을 활용해 Mamba-2의 순전파(forward pass) 커널을 고성능으로 구현하는 방법을 다룬다.
items.why_it_matters: 저수준 CUDA 커널 작성 없이 Python만으로 고성능 GPU 커널을 만들 수 있다면, Mamba류 구조적 상태공간 모델(SSM) 같은 최신 아키텍처의 실험·배포 진입장벽이 크게 낮아진다.
items.whats_different: 기존 CUDA C++ 수준의 스레드·워프 스케줄링 관리 대비, cuTile은 타일 단위 primitive로 이를 추상화하고 컴파일러가 최적화를 자동 수행한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Relational Learning as World Modeling
items.abstract: Relational learning typically predicts from a database state, but decision making asks a different question: how will that state change under an action? In operational systems, the answer depends on system-specific dynamics that may not be visible in the database itself. We view each such system as a relational "world" and ask whether a model can infer how it behaves from observed executions. We introduce TabWM (Tabular World Model) and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given executions from an unseen world, TabWM uses them as context to predict the sparse structured edits caused by a new action without parameter updates. Across 512 held-out worlds, complete-edit F1 rises from 0.016 with no observed executions to 0.685 with 64, where a correct edit must match its operation, relational location, and value. Because these predictions are explicit relational edits, they can be applied recursively to imagine candidate futures and compare actions before they are taken. Broader search over these predicted futures improves the realized return of selected action sequences. Together, these results suggest that relational dynamics can be learned in context, broadening relational learning from modeling system state to modeling how that state changes under action.
items.title_ko: TabWM, 관계형 세계모델 제시 — 실행 64회 관찰만으로 edit F1 0.016→0.685 상승
items.summary: 이 논문은 관계형 학습을 데이터베이스 상태 예측에서 '행동에 따른 상태 변화 예측'으로 확장한다. 저자들은 각 운영 시스템을 관계형 '월드'로 보고, 사전학습용 실행 가능 관계형 월드 생성기 WorldRel과 이를 활용하는 TabWM(Tabular World Model)을 제안한다. TabWM은 미지의 월드에서 관찰된 실행들을 맥락으로 삼아 파라미터 업데이트 없이 새로운 행동이 유발하는 희소 구조적 edit을 예측한다. 512개의 held-out 월드에서 실행 관찰 0회일 때 edit F1 0.016이던 것이 64회 관찰 시 **0.685**로 상승했으며, 정답 edit은 연산·관계형 위치·값이 모두 일치해야 한다. 예측된 edit은 재귀적으로 적용해 미래 상태를 상상하고 행동을 비교하는 데 쓰이며, 이를 통한 탐색 확장은 선택된 행동열의 실현 보상을 향상시킨다.
items.why_it_matters: 관계형 데이터 기반 의사결정 시스템에서 '행동이 상태를 어떻게 바꾸는가'를 맥락 학습만으로 예측할 수 있다면, 시스템별 동역학을 몰라도 행동 계획과 시뮬레이션이 가능해진다는 점에서 의미가 크다.
items.whats_different: 기존 관계형 학습이 데이터베이스 상태 자체를 예측하는 데 그쳤던 것과 달리, TabWM은 파라미터 업데이트 없이 관찰된 실행만으로 **행동에 따른 구조적 edit**을 추론해 미래 상태를 재귀적으로 시뮬레이션한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: MOSS-Image Technical Report
items.abstract: Recent closed-source image generation systems can produce diverse visual content from simple compositions to information-dense graphics, yet open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts. To narrow this gap, we introduce MOSS-Image, an open generation system that combines high-fidelity visual synthesis with intent-aware composition. First, we pretrain a 5B single-stream diffusion transformer (DiT) from scratch with a carefully designed recipe, enabling bilingual long-form text rendering and precise layout control. Second, we develop an intention-aware agentic prompt enhancement (PE) module that translates diverse user requests into detailed content and layout specifications. Together, they enable MOSS-Image to generate text-rich and layout-coherent images. We further introduce LongLongTextBench (LLTB) for evaluating long-form English and Chinese text rendering, and RealLayoutArena (RLA) for end-to-end layout-rich generation. MOSS-Image achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-weight models on LLTB, with an average text coverage of 96.3%. On RLA, MOSS-Image ranks second in the end-to-end system comparison, while its backbone ranks first among generators evaluated with shared enhanced prompts. We will release the model, training recipe, and evaluation framework to support further research and promote the text-to-image community.
items.title_ko: MOSS-Image 공개 — 5B DiT로 밀도 높은 텍스트·레이아웃 이미지 생성, LLTB 텍스트 커버리지 96.3%
items.summary: MOSS-Image는 고밀도 텍스트와 복잡한 레이아웃 생성에 취약한 오픈 가중치 텍스트-이미지 모델의 한계를 보완하기 위해 제안된 오픈 생성 시스템이다. 처음부터 사전학습한 **5B 단일 스트림 확산 트랜스포머(DiT)**를 통해 이중언어 장문 텍스트 렌더링과 정밀 레이아웃 제어를 지원하며, 사용자 요청을 세부 콘텐츠·레이아웃 명세로 변환하는 의도 인식 에이전트형 프롬프트 강화(PE) 모듈을 결합했다. 장문 텍스트 렌더링 평가용 LongLongTextBench(LLTB)와 레이아웃 중심 생성 평가용 RealLayoutArena(RLA)라는 두 벤치마크도 함께 제안했다. LLTB에서 오픈 가중치 모델 중 최고 성능으로 **평균 텍스트 커버리지 96.3%**를 달성했고, RLA에서는 엔드투엔드 비교 2위, 동일 강화 프롬프트 기준 생성기 자체 성능은 1위를 기록했다. 모델, 학습 레시피, 평가 프레임워크를 모두 공개할 예정이다.
items.why_it_matters: 텍스트가 밀집된 그래픽이나 복잡한 레이아웃 생성은 폐쇄형 모델이 독점하던 영역이었는데, 이를 오픈 가중치로 재현 가능하게 한다는 점에서 텍스트-이미지 생성 생태계 전반에 영향을 줄 수 있다. 모델과 평가 프레임워크를 함께 공개함으로써 재현 연구와 후속 벤치마킹이 용이해진다는 점도 주목할 만하다.
items.whats_different: 기존 오픈 가중치 텍스트-이미지 모델들이 밀도 높은 텍스트·정교한 레이아웃 처리에서 어려움을 겪던 것과 달리, MOSS-Image는 처음부터 설계된 5B DiT와 의도 인식 프롬프트 강화 모듈을 결합해 이 격차를 좁혔다.

items.title: MorphAct: Robot Policies Morphing with the Worlds They Act In
items.abstract: Progress toward general intelligence in the physical world requires scaling robot learning across diverse environments and interactions. However, existing robot policies use shared parameters that remain fixed across interaction contexts. When different operations favor competing parameter adjustments, fitting their mixture can leave individual operations insufficiently adapted. Our atomic-task diagnostics reveal competing update directions in both vision-language and action parameters, with source-improving updates increasing loss on other tasks. This motivates MorphAct, a contextual parameterization framework that dynamically adjusts robot policy parameters as interaction contexts change. Two coupled generators produce context-dependent low-rank updates for the vision-language and action modules. Their coupling follows the policy's computational dependency: vision-language updates shape the representations that condition action-side parameter generation. Both generators are trained jointly through the native action objective, without operation labels or expert-adapter targets. MorphAct improves performance across three VLA backbones on LIBERO and Meta-World, with gains of up to 16.30%. In real-world evaluation, it achieves gains of up to 14% over π_{0.5}. Ablations support the benefits of contextual parameter generation and representation coupling.
items.title_ko: MorphAct, 로봇 정책을 맥락별로 동적 조정 — LIBERO·Meta-World서 최대 16.30%, 실세계서 π_{0.5} 대비 14% 향상
items.summary: 기존 로봇 정책은 상호작용 맥락이 달라져도 고정된 공유 파라미터를 사용하는데, 저자들은 원자적 과제 진단을 통해 비전-언어 및 액션 파라미터에서 서로 충돌하는 업데이트 방향이 존재함을 확인했다. 한 과제를 개선하는 업데이트가 다른 과제의 손실을 증가시키는 현상이 그 증거다. 이를 해결하기 위해 **MorphAct**라는 맥락 의존적 파라미터화 프레임워크를 제안하며, 두 개의 결합된 생성기가 비전-언어 모듈과 액션 모듈에 대해 맥락별 저랭크 업데이트를 생성한다. 두 생성기는 정책의 계산적 의존 관계를 따라 결합되며(비전-언어 업데이트가 액션측 파라미터 생성을 위한 표현을 형성), 별도의 과제 라벨이나 전문가 어댑터 타겟 없이 네이티브 액션 목표로 공동 학습된다. 세 가지 VLA 백본에서 LIBERO와 Meta-World 벤치마크 기준 최대 **16.30%** 성능 향상을, 실세계 평가에서는 π_{0.5} 대비 최대 14% 향상을 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: 로봇 정책이 다양한 환경과 상호작용으로 확장될수록 고정 파라미터 공유 방식의 한계가 드러나는데, 이 연구는 맥락별 동적 파라미터 생성이 범용 로봇 지능 확장의 실질적 병목을 해소할 수 있음을 보여준다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 고정 공유 파라미터 정책이나 별도의 전문가 어댑터·과제 라벨에 의존하는 방식과 달리, **별도 라벨 없이** 비전-언어·액션 모듈 간 계산적 의존성을 반영한 결합 생성기로 맥락별 저랭크 업데이트를 직접 학습한다.

items.title: AI Changed How We Code. It Hasn’t Changed How We Work Together.
items.abstract: This summer, I built a small experiment called ContextCue . The idea came from something I kept seeing during my internship. The engineers around me were using AI everywhere in the software development process. GitHub Copilot and Claude models helped with specs, code, reviews, and tests. The team also maintained reusable skills that taught coding agents how the team worked. One of those skills could take a UI design and turn it into working frontend code. The code was moving faster, but the understanding around the code did not seem to move faster with it. The software was being built by nine teams spread across three continents, with one team working closely with the customer. A request might begin in a customer conversation, move through one team, then reach another team several time zones away. By the time the work reached engineering, some of the original meaning could be missing. That was the problem I wanted ContextCue to explore. ContextCue takes recorded meetings and tries to preserve more than a transcript or summary. It keeps the spoken discussion, important visual context from the screen, the decisions that were made, the reasons behind them, and the source they came from. The goal is to create a shared piece of context that can move with the work from one team to another. It is still an experiment, but the problem behind it felt very real. As far as I could see, a lot of time in distributed software teams went into reaching a common understanding before the coding even started. AI was already helping with the final stages of software development. I wanted to see whether it could help earlier, while teams were still trying to understand what they were building and why. Where the context disappears Meetings were already being recorded, and tools like Microsoft Teams could produce an AI summary. On my team, that summary often arrived as an email and stayed there. That worked well enough for the people who attended the meeting. It was less useful for the team that picked up the work later, especially if that team was in another country and had not seen the original conversation. There were two other problems. A summary usually covered one meeting, while the understanding behind a feature was often built across several. Different teams might discuss the same request days apart, each adding a new constraint or interpretation. A transcript could also miss important visual context. Many of our conversations involved screen sharing. Someone might point at a page and say, “This is too slow,” or highlight a part of a workflow while explaining what needed to change. The words alone did not always carry the meaning. That is where I started thinking about context as something larger than a transcript. A simple example Imagine that a customer asks for a “faster report.” During the call, the customer shares a screen, points at a page that is slow to open, and explains that managers use it every morning before a meeting. Everyone on that call understands that “faster” means the page should open more quickly. Two days later, another team in another time zone discusses the same request. Nobody in that meeting saw the original screen. They read “faster report” as “the report should finish running sooner” and begin planning backend work. Both meeting summaries might contain the same phrase: Make the report faster. Nothing in that sentence shows that the two teams mean different things. The problem only becomes visible when the customer sees the result. This is a simple example, but it captures the issue I kept noticing. Requirements move through people before they ever become code. If the meaning changes during that process, AI can help a team implement the wrong interpretation very efficiently. The sports version of the same problem Sports gave me another way to think about it. Imagine a soccer match where a player misses a late chance to score a goal. The match report can record the shot, the player, the minute, and whether it was on
items.title_ko: 인턴 경험담 — AI는 코딩 속도를 높였지만 분산 팀 간 '이해의 공유'는 그대로, ContextCue 실험 소개
items.summary: 필자는 인턴십 중 3개 대륙 9개 팀이 협업하는 소프트웨어 개발에서 GitHub Copilot과 Claude 등 AI 도구가 스펙 작성, 코드, 리뷰, 테스트 전반에 쓰이지만 코드 작성 속도에 비해 요구사항에 대한 이해는 팀 간에 제대로 전달되지 않는 문제를 목격했다. 고객과의 대화에서 시작된 요청이 여러 팀을 거치며 원래 의미를 잃는 경우가 많았는데, 예컨대 '더 빠른 리포트'라는 표현이 화면 공유 맥락 없이는 '페이지 로딩 속도'와 '백엔드 처리 속도'로 서로 다르게 해석될 수 있었다. 기존 회의록 요약은 한 번의 회의만 다루고 화면 공유 중 가리킨 시각적 맥락을 놓치는 한계가 있었다. 이를 해결하기 위해 필자는 **ContextCue**라는 실험적 도구를 만들어, 녹화된 회의에서 음성 논의뿐 아니라 화면상의 시각적 맥락, 결정 사항과 그 근거, 출처까지 보존해 여러 팀에 걸쳐 이동 가능한 공유 컨텍스트를 생성하고자 했다.
items.why_it_matters: AI가 코딩 자체는 빠르게 만들었지만, 잘못 전달된 요구사항을 매우 효율적으로 '잘못 구현'하게 만들 위험이 있다는 점은 분산 팀 협업에서 AI 도입 전략을 재고하게 만든다.
items.whats_different: 기존 **Microsoft Teams AI 요약** 같은 도구는 단일 회의 단위로 텍스트 요약만 제공해 여러 회의에 걸친 맥락 축적과 화면 공유 중 시각적 의미를 놓치는 반면, ContextCue는 음성·시각 맥락·결정 근거·출처를 함께 보존해 팀 간 이동 가능한 컨텍스트로 만들고자 한다.

items.title: Recognition Is Not Grounding: Benchmarking Multilingual Financial Evidence Extraction
items.abstract: Comparing financial disclosures across languages requires identifying shared accounting concepts and recovering all numerical facts that express them. Existing benchmarks evaluate aspects of these capabilities, but provide limited insight into whether both succeed on the same multilingual evidence. In particular, it remains unclear whether language models can recognize these concepts across languages and exhaustively recover their corresponding numerical evidence from the same contexts. We introduce MULTIFINGROUND, a benchmark designed to investigate this recognition-grounding gap in multilingual financial reports. Constructed from FY2025 disclosures of 90 issuers in English, French, and Greek, MULTIFINGROUND aligns independently authored reports through a shared accounting taxonomy and provides traceable fact-level annotations. The benchmark evaluates financial fact identification, concept recognition, exhaustive fact selection, and concept discrimination without candidate labels. Across 15 evaluated models, eight API and open-weight reference models achieve 97.3-99.4\% concept recognition accuracy, yet miss at least one target fact in 26.6-41.9\% of correctly recognized groups. Further analyses reveal substantial variation in concept discrimination and limited gains from the evaluated finance-specialized models. Our findings demonstrate that strong concept recognition can coexist with incomplete evidence recovery, highlighting the importance of evaluating semantic recognition and evidence completeness together.
items.title_ko: MULTIFINGROUND 공개 — 개념인식 97~99% 모델도 수치증거 추출은 26~42% 누락
items.summary: 다국어 재무공시 비교를 위해서는 동일한 회계 개념을 인식하고 이를 뒷받침하는 모든 수치 근거를 빠짐없이 찾아내야 한다. 연구진은 영어, 프랑스어, 그리스어로 작성된 90개 발행사의 2025회계연도 공시를 공통 회계 분류체계로 정렬하고, 사실 단위로 추적 가능한 주석을 단 벤치마크 MULTIFINGROUND를 공개했다. 이 벤치마크는 재무 사실 식별, 개념 인식, 후보 라벨 없는 완전한 사실 선택 및 개념 구분 능력을 평가한다. 15개 모델 중 API·오픈웨이트 기준모델 8개는 **97.3~99.4%의 개념 인식 정확도**를 보였지만, 올바르게 인식된 그룹에서도 **26.6~41.9%는 최소 하나의 목표 사실을 누락**했다. 금융 특화 모델도 큰 개선을 보이지 않았으며, 개념 구분 능력에는 상당한 편차가 나타났다.
items.why_it_matters: 개념을 정확히 인식하는 것과 그 증거를 빠짐없이 모으는 것은 별개의 능력임을 보여주며, 재무 분석 등 완전성이 중요한 업무에 LLM을 적용할 때 의미 인식만으로는 신뢰할 수 없다는 점을 시사한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 벤치마크들은 개념 인식이나 사실 추출 중 한 측면만 평가했던 것과 달리, MULTIFINGROUND는 동일한 다국어 맥락에서 인식과 증거 완전성을 함께 측정해 '인식-근거화 격차'를 드러낸다.
